text:
Adin Hill spent last season fighting the puck: 15 goals below expected in 27 games, the kind of year that makes you wonder about a goalie's job. This season looks like a reset. He is 7-2-1 with a .907 save rate and has saved 3.0 goals above expected, meaning he has kept out three more goals than the shots against him would usually allow (70th percentile among goalies).

The trend is better than the total. One bad night in St. Louis (six goals on Oct. 22) still sits in his numbers, but over his last five starts he is 5.39 goals above expected, including a strong game in Buffalo on Nov. 8 and an overtime game against Nashville in which The Athletic's Jesse Granger wrote that he was "outstanding" late to keep it tied. The thing to watch is the hardest chances: his .667 on high-danger shots is a little below the league's .685, and that's where the Cup-winning version of Hill (2023) made his name.
